_comment: Narration for the Duum demo (out/duum/cut.mp4). Each cue names the BEAT it lands on, from that scene's .beats.jsonl, so the voice tracks the picture. Budgeted at Brian's MEASURED 2.9 words/sec (from the UnoDOS OS demo). Claims checked against source: DUUM.PY is Python on PYRT/MicroPython; uno.read_at streams the WAD lump-by-lump (never slurped); render() (BSP walk + column loop) is Python, cv.wall_span/mask_span/flat_span are C; monster AI + weapons + E1M1-E1M9 exist. REFILMED 2026-08-18 on FREEDOOM (BSD), so nothing licensed is in the published film; Freedoom ships ORIGINAL maps, so the footage is an interior corridor and NOT id's courtyard. Two claims were retired with that change: the SKY (no sky sector is on the new route) and 'former humans' (id's monster name). This take does land a clean framed kill, which the id-WAD takes never could.
_voice: Brian - Deep, Resonant and Comforting (matches arin's UnoDOS OS demo)

cues.text: This is Doom, running inside UnoDOS - and written entirely in Python.
It runs as an ordinary app, on the operating system's own Python runtime.
It streams a real Doom game file, never loading it whole.
Walls, floors and ceilings, drawn perspective correct.
The zombies shoot back, and your health drops as you push down the corridor.
Weapons, monsters and pickups, across all nine levels of the first episode.
Only the per-pixel drawing is C. The geometry and the game logic are Python.
Every other port of this system rebuilds its own apps in each machine's language.
Duum does the reverse - a whole outside game engine, in nothing but Python.
